description: Tame in a way nothing wild is: it comes closer than it should, bolts, and bites in earnest when it cannot run.
lore: The white is a poor idea in country that has things hunting in it, and the coat comes away with the cold still in it: a burr of fur, blue down in its shadows, that takes its time finishing the thaw in your palm. None of that is the strange part. The strange part is that it comes toward you.

Nothing wild does that. A rabbit is an animal that has decided in advance about every noise there is, and this one decides correctly about all of them, and then for a moment decides wrong. It drifts three or four steps in your direction with its ears up, the way an animal moves toward a person it is expecting something from, and then whatever is left inside catches up with it and it is forty feet away. Watch that happen twice and you know a thing about it that it does not know about itself. Somebody kept this one, and whoever it was got forgotten before the rabbit did.

The rest of what it does is a routine with the middle taken out. Twice a day it comes onto the same patch of open ground, faces the same way, and waits. Nothing arrives. After a while it goes and eats. People who have sat and watched it will tell you the hour is exact, and not one of them can tell you what the hour was for, and neither can it. Loyalty would need somebody in there to be loyal; what is keeping the appointment is the shape a loyalty leaves behind, still perfectly on time. It has also put by a store of hard brown kernels, which was never a rabbit's food. Half the small things in the low country are hoarding something they cannot eat.

It bolts from everything, which is why people underestimate it, and it will not turn while it still has somewhere to run. Take that away and it turns. The teeth are real and were always real, and there is no gentler lesson available in this country than the one a white rabbit hands somebody in their first season, which is that nearly everything here will hurt you eventually and almost none of it means to.

An animal that never fought anything in its existence is nonetheless the finest authority in the world on weight: how much roof will hold, how far a thing can drop and still run, what to do about the weight coming down. That turns out to be what the stone is — a plate of grey granite seamed with salmon pink, the exact pink of the inside of its ears, which people notice and then decide not to make anything of. Worked into armour it does for whoever wears it what the burrow did for the rabbit. Falls come off shorter. The blow meant to crush arrives merely heavy.
